answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, association only — 1989 cross-section):
Among young NLSY79 respondents in the 1989 cross-section (ages 24–32), being older is modestly negatively associated with the likelihood of being a net dissaver (withdrawing more from savings than putting in, DISSAVED=1). In the headline logistic model controlling for income, gender, BMI and race, each additional year of age is associated with ~4.7% lower odds of DISSAVED=1 (OR ≈ 0.95, 95% CI 0.935–0.970) and with roughly 1 percentage point lower probability (average marginal effect ≈ −0.96 pp/year; predicted probability falls from ≈25.3% at age 24 to ≈18.4% at age 32, holding other covariates at their means). The age gradient is weakly non-linear — a shallow peak around the mid-20s (≈25–27) followed by a steeper decline into the early 30s (quadratic term p ≈ 0.046) — and the overall association is small (model pseudo R² ≈ 0.006), so it should be read as a modest, associative pattern confined to the 24–32 window. Read through a time-preference lens, net dissaving is a proxy for higher discounting/lower patience, so the gradient is consistent with older youth being slightly more patient savers, though the effect is too small to be economically large.

FULL EVIDENCE (all from executed final_analysis.py):

(i) HEADLINE logistic — DISSAVED ~ AGE_c + AGE2_c + LOGINC + BMI + MALE + BLACK + HISPANIC (n=12,686), age centered at 27.86:
   AGE_c    coef -0.0485  OR 0.9526 [0.9353, 0.9703]  p<0.001
   AGE2_c   coef -0.0087  OR 0.9914 [0.9829, 0.9998]  p=0.046
   LOGINC   coef +0.1194  OR 1.1268 [1.0747, 1.1814]  p<0.001
   BMI      coef +0.0040  OR 1.0040 [0.9972, 1.0108]  p=0.250 (ns)
   MALE     coef -0.1998  OR 0.8189 [0.7539, 0.8894]  p<0.001
   BLACK    coef +0.2051  OR 1.2276 [1.1132, 1.3539]  p<0.001
   HISPANIC coef +0.1002  OR 1.1054 [0.9837, 1.2422]  p=0.092 (ns)
   Pseudo R² = 0.0061

   SENSITIVITY — no INCOME (same spec minus LOGINC):
   AGE_c coef -0.0430 OR 0.9579 [0.9406,0.9755] p<0.001; AGE2_c p=0.051; Pseudo R²=0.0043.
   → Age effect is robust: with income (controlled) OR 0.953/yr; without income (total) OR 0.958/yr. Nearly identical — income is not a large suppressor of the age association here.

   SENSITIVITY — headline spec with BMI winsorized at 99th pct:
   AGE_c -0.0487 (OR 0.9525), AGE2_c p=0.047 → age coefficients essentially unchanged; BMI outliers do not drive the result.

(ii) Average marginal effect of a +1 yr age increase on P(DISSAVED=1) [headline] = −0.00963 (≈ −0.96 pp/yr); per 5-yr increment ≈ −0.048 (−4.8 pp).

(iii) Predicted P(DISSAVED=1) at mean covariates: age 24 = 0.2529, age 28 = 0.2408, age 32 = 0.1837.

(iv) Non-parametric observed DISSAVED rate by age:
   24y 25.5% | 25y 24.1% | 26y 25.8% | 27y 26.3% | 28y 24.1% | 29y 23.3% | 30y 20.2% | 31y 21.6% | 32y 18.2%
   → shallow hump peaking ~26–27, then declining; matches the fitted curve's peak (~age 25) and steeper late decline.

(v) Quadratic-vs-linear Wald test (AGE2_c = 0): chi2 = 3.983, p = 0.0460 → significant at the 0.05 level (marginal), so the quadratic is retained as primary per your guidance.

(vi) Supplementary SAMESAVE-conditional estimand (distinct from the headline):
   P(DISSAVED=1 | SAMESAVE=0) = 0.3782 (n=7,901) vs P(DISSAVED=1) full sample = 0.2355 (n=12,686).
   Within SAMESAVE=0, conditional logistic AGE_c coef = −0.0901 (p<0.001), pseudo R²=0.0486 — the age association is roughly twice as strong once restricted to those whose savings actually changed, reinforcing the direction of the headline.

Diagnostics / limitations:
• AGE terms well-identified after centering (VIF AGE_c=1.02, AGE2_c=2.10). Moderate multicollinearity between LOGINC (VIF 9.3) and BMI (VIF 10.3) does not affect the age terms.
• Effect is statistically significant but small in magnitude (pseudo R²≈0.006; ~1 pp/yr).
• Cross-section ⇒ association only, no causality. Age window 24–32 only; no extrapolation. Curvature is weakly identified over 9 years.

payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_bmi_processed.csv (12,686 rows, 0 missing). Constructed centered age AGE_c and AGE2_c (resolves raw AGE/AGE_2 collinearity, VIF 686->~1), log1p(INCOME), MALE dummy, winsorized BMI. Fitted (a) headline logistic DISSAVED ~ AGE_c+AGE2_c+LOGINC+BMI+MALE+BLACK+HISPANIC, (b) no-income sensitivity, (c) BMI-winsorized sensitivity. Computed average marginal effect of +1 yr age, predicted P at ages 24/28/32 at mean covariates, per-age observed rates, quadratic-vs-linear Wald test, and supplementary P(DISSAVED=1|SAMESAVE=0). Association only (1989 cross-section).
